args.title: corvid-msa-counter-redline-cover-note.docx
args.body:
CORVID ANALYTICS MSA — COUNTER-REDLINE COVER NOTE

Prepared for: Northgale Systems, Inc. (Customer)
Prepared by: Harrow & Vane LLP
Re: Corvid Analytics LLC rev B counter-draft of Northgale client-form Master Services Agreement (v2 execution-ready base)
Basis: Northgale Systems, Inc. Commercial Contracting Playbook, 2026 Edition (the "Playbook")
Date: July 2026

This cover note accompanies Northgale's counter-turn redline to the operative Corvid rev B counter-draft transmitted by Dahlgren & Pike LLP on 9 July 2026. We respond to every tracked change in rev B by reference to the 2026 Playbook. For each change we state whether Northgale ACCEPTS the change, COUNTERS at a Playbook-approved fallback, or REJECTS the change, together with the specific figures our counter-turn will carry. Positions that exceed a Playbook floor or standard and that lack an approved fallback are noted as requiring escalation and are addressed separately in the escalation/board-approval package.

1. Section 2.2 — Renewal period.
Corvid rev B: successive two (2) year renewal periods (client form: successive one (1) year periods).
Position: REJECT.
Playbook PB-1 provides no approved fallback for multi-year renewal periods of any length; multi-year renewal is out of policy and requires Chief Legal Officer (CLO) approval. Our counter-turn reverts to the client-form standard of automatic renewal in successive one (1) year periods. Counter figure: one (1) year renewal periods. This is an out-of-policy ask requiring escalation (CLO approval).

2. Section 4.3 — Late-interest rate.
Corvid rev B: 1.5% per month on late undisputed amounts (client form: 1.0% per month).
Position: COUNTER at Playbook standard.
Playbook PB-4 states late interest never above 1.0% per month. We counter at the maximum the Playbook permits. Counter figure: 1.0% per month on late undisputed amounts.

3. NEW Section 4.4 — Suspension of services for non-payment.
Corvid rev B (new provision): Provider may suspend Services if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date until all past-due amounts are paid in full.
Position: COUNTER at Playbook-approved condition (suspension rights are otherwise out of policy).
Playbook PB-4 permits suspension rights only if preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice, and requires Chief Financial Officer (CFO) sign-off for any suspension right of any kind. Our counter-turn will accept a suspension right only on those conditions. Counter figures: any suspension right must be preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice; suspension right of any kind subject to CFO sign-off. The fifteen (15) day trigger is rejected; we counter with the thirty (30) day cure-notice condition.

4. Section 7.2 — Termination for convenience notice period.
Corvid rev B: ninety (90) days' prior written notice (client form: thirty (30) days).
Position: COUNTER at Playbook-approved fallback.
Playbook PB-2 sets the Standard at thirty (30) days and the Approved fallback at up to forty-five (45) days; any notice period above forty-five (45) days requires CLO approval. Corvid's ninety (90) day ask exceeds the fallback. We counter at the approved fallback. Counter figure: forty-five (45) days' prior written notice for a termination for convenience.

5. NEW Section 7.4 — Wind-down period and compensation.
Corvid rev B (new provision): upon any termination other than for Provider's uncured material breach, a sixty (60) day wind-down period applies during which Customer pays the full monthly base service fee for wind-down services plus all committed third-party costs.
Position: COUNTER at Playbook-approved terms.
Playbook PB-3 permits a wind-down only if (i) capped at thirty (30) days and (ii) compensation is limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments; full-fee wind-down compensation is out of policy. We counter accordingly. Counter figures: wind-down period of thirty (30) days; compensation limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments (full-fee compensation rejected).

6. Section 9.1 — Liability-cap measurement period.
Corvid rev B: cap measured at fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim (client form: twenty-four (24) months).
Position: COUNTER at Playbook-approved fallback floor.
Playbook PB-5 sets the Standard cap at twenty-four (24) months with an Approved fallback floor of eighteen (18) months; a twelve (12) month measurement period is below the fallback floor and requires CLO approval. We counter at the approved fallback floor. Counter figure: eighteen (18) months' measurement period.

7. Section 9.2 — Liability-cap carve-out treatment.
Corvid rev B: deletes clause (c), subjecting gross negligence and willful misconduct to the Section 9.1 cap.
Position: REJECT.
Playbook PB-5 treats the carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct as non-negotiable; deletion of any carve-out requires joint CLO and CFO approval. We reject the deletion and retain clause (c) so that gross negligence and willful misconduct remain outside the cap. Counter figure: retain the Section 9.2(c) carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct. This is an out-of-policy ask requiring escalation (joint CLO and CFO approval).

8. Section 11.2 — Service-credit cap percentage.
Corvid rev B: aggregate cap of 10% of the monthly base service fee per month (client form: 20%).
Position: COUNTER at Playbook-approved fallback floor.
Playbook PB-6 sets the Standard aggregate monthly credit cap at 20% with an Approved fallback floor of 15%; a 10% aggregate credit cap is out of policy. We counter at the approved fallback floor. Counter figure: 15% aggregate monthly service-credit cap.

All other terms of the client form v2 not modified by rev B are accepted as drafted. Items 1 (renewal) and 7 (carve-out deletion) are out-of-policy asks that breach a Playbook standard/floor or lack an approved fallback and are escalated for approval as separately directed. Please direct any substantive questions to our firm; we will copy Deputy GC on calls with Dahlgren & Pike.

— Harrow & Vane LLP, for Northgale Systems, Inc.
